NOTE the missing bare 'cataract' alias: it scored 66.7 against the query 'Cardiac CT' -- 'cardiacct' and 'cataract' are near-anagrams -- which cleared CLARIFY_THRESHOLD and turned Story 8 / Demo Script #5's honest miss into a clarifying question. Nothing is lost by dropping it, because a bare 'cataract' query is a token subset of 'cataract surgery' and still scores 100. Lexical, not semantic: the matcher cannot tell an eye from a heart, so a new alias can collide with a demo-critical honest-miss string by pure spelling accident. tests/unit/test_rate_matcher.py builds its catalog from this file, so the suite catches this class on every reseed.

See the schema comment in 0001_init_schema.sql.
_note: Why this file exists in this shape, and the two rules that keep it honest. (1) Every negotiated_rate must equal the corresponding cell in db/seed/source/rate_sheet_2026.xlsx -- enforced by tests/unit/test_rate_sheet_source.py, which fails on any drift, any sheet procedure missing from the seed, and any seeded procedure that is not on the sheet. Before that test existed, 8 of the 11 shared rates had drifted, 4 sheet procedures were missing, and 3 procedures were seeded that Meridian never negotiated -- the numeric-provenance guardrail passed all of them, because it proves a figure came from a tool and cannot prove the tool's table was real. (2) search_aliases are OURS, not the sheet's: they are the app's search vocabulary and are not diffed against the xlsx. One deliberate omission -- no alias anywhere contains the word 'cardiac', because Story 8 / Demo Script #5 requires 'Cardiac CT' to be a clean NOT_ON_FILE, and giving 93306 a 'cardiac ultrasound' alias would score it into the clarify band and turn an honest miss into a question. A CSR typing 'cardiac ultrasound' therefore gets an honest miss rather than a wrong match, which is the safe direction to fail.
